content.title: For builders: Detailed changes coming in 2026
content.summary: In 2026, the City of Arvada will implement significant updates to its building codes, focusing on community resiliency, compliance options, and advancements in building technology. Key changes include provisions for tiny homes, 3D printed homes, and accessory dwelling units, as well as enhanced fire safety, energy efficiency, and climate resilience measures. The updates will also adopt the Colorado Model Low Energy Carbon Code, emphasizing decarbonization and electric vehicle readiness.
content.body:
As the City of Arvada [updates its building codes in 2026](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1388/14791/New-Building-Codes-2026), a number of changes are coming that will impact builders, designers, developers, homeowners, and business owners. Below is more detailed information about what's changing.

## Summary: Building code updates

As Arvada changes and grows, and as we learn from those changes, building codes change too. You will see this clearly in the building code updates for Arvada.

These new Building codes will have an emphasis on resiliency for our community, new options for code compliance, new provisions to help Arvada adapt to new innovations in building technology, needed fixes to provide better clarity for compliance, decarbonization and electrification, and updated provisions to face new hazards in our built environments.

Some notable significant changes include appendices for tiny homes and 3D printed homes to help our community grow in more sustainable and innovative ways and provisions that provide new options for home, dwelling unit, and sleeping room construction (such as sleeping lofts, habitable attics, 3D printed homes, and accessory dwelling units, or ADUs). New innovations in construction continue to progress, which is clear in this code adoption with new allowances and requirements for A2L refrigerants, improved accessibility and usability of the building codes, improved accessibility requirements for accessible and useable buildings and facilities, enhanced fire safety, energy storage, energy efficiency, climate resilience, and advanced new material options for compliance.

The list of newly adopted codes includes:

- 2024 International Building Code (IBC)
- 2024 International Residential Code (IRC)
- 2024 International Fire Code (IFC)
- 2024 International Existing Building Code (IEBC)
- 2024 International Plumbing Code (IPC)
- 2024 International Mechanical Code (IMC)
- 2024 International Fuel Gas Code (IFGC)
- 2024 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code (ISPSC)
- 2024 International Property Maintenance Code (IPMC)
- The Colorado Model Low Energy Carbon Code, based on the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code (IECC)
- Arvada Wildfire Resiliency Code
- 2017 ICC A117.1 Accessible and Useable Buildings and Facilities (ANSI- Adopted by reference through the IBC)
- Newest version of the National Electrical Code, 2026 (also known as the NFPA 70; published by the National Fire Protection Agency)

Please note that the 2023 National Electrical Code will remain the electrical code for the City of Arvada, however the City does expect to begin implementing the 2026 NEC later on in 2026, when the State of Colorado begins implementation. Further updates surrounding this transition will be shared on this page as we get closer to the new electrical code implementation. [Read more about the full changes in this list of significant changes prepared by the City](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1461/Building-Code-Adoption-Significant-Chang).

You can also read more about the changes from the ICC in [this free resource](https://codes.iccsafe.org/codes/i-codes/2024-icodes) or by purchasing [this book of significant changes](https://codes.iccsafe.org/codes/resources/significant-changes).

## Summary: Energy code updates

As part of this process, we will be adopting the Colorado Model Low Energy Carbon Code, based on the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code to comply with the state minimum mandates for electric vehicle (EV)-ready, electric-ready, and solar-ready provisions. 

There are some real benefits to these changes: This code has a focus on decarbonization and is one of the first in the nation to require demand response controls. These controls are capable of automatically shutting off electrical consumption when not in use, providing more options for compliance and helping reduce construction costs by allowing flexibility and more affordable pathways to compliance. These changes will help us meet community-wide goals for reduction in GHG emissions. Additionally, some of these changes provide for ongoing energy cost savings for homes. To read more about other changes with this code and benefits, please visit the [Significant changes page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1461/Building-Code-Adoption-Significant-Chang).

Read more about the [Model Low Energy Carbon Code](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11o5GTqFXWHj03ubR_Sk2bGQ_UWXOstRJ3qQh1oUXwFI/edit?tab=t.0) or check out [this article from Colorado Energy Office](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11o5GTqFXWHj03ubR_Sk2bGQ_UWXOstRJ3qQh1oUXwFI/edit?tab=t.0).

## Summary: Wildfire code updates

In addition, we are mandated to adopt a wildfire resiliency code and have created our own Arvada Wildfire Resiliency Code. This code requires defensible space and structural hardening to help mitigate wildfire risk. It applies to buildings and structures in areas of Arvada where the fire intensity classification is a low or high risk and will impact many parts of the community. A wildfire map will show these levels of fire intensity based on local and state maps and current and historical conditions within our community. 

If your property falls in one of these zones and you are planning to build an addition, detached structure, deck or patio cover, or if you are reroofing or residing, then you may be subject to additional structural hardening requirements, and in some cases, defensible space requirements for a certain distance away from your home. Read about the [State Wildfire Resiliency Code](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bhSESWE9pei6MMsv52VeGtC_WBgD7bVA/view?usp=sharing) and read more about what will be impacted for you in the [Arvada Wildfire Resiliency Code FAQ](https://www.arvadaco.gov/m/faq?cat=105).

## Questions?

The City of Arvada is committed to helping our building community understand and implement these changes. Stay tuned for more information on opportunities to ask questions and learn more. If you have questions about any of the upcoming changes, please do not hesitate to reach out to the Building Division at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#610314080d05080f061104130c081512210013170005004f0e1306).
